thread:
inc-bot: INCIDENT 3372104567 — P1: Dedicated pool 'ellipsia-prod' reporting GPU exhaustion for single enterprise tenant (Ellipsia Corp). Auto-alert triggered: queue depth high, tail latency spike. Paging oncall.

sarah-oncall: I’m taking this. seeing 100% GPU util across 6 nodes, queue depth ~820, 99th latency > 4s. Confirming customer impact (Ellipsia) - they're on a single-tenant reserved pool, no multi-tenant sharding in place.

mike-sre: noted. Are autoscaler logs showing any recent scale events?

sarah-oncall: autoscaler attempted, but backoff + pinned node config prevented new allocations. Looks like pool has max_pool_size=6 and tenant pinned_nodes=6. no room to scale.

julia-eng: tagging runtime: could we trigger emergency burst (manual) or evict best-effort workloads?

omar-obs: metrics: rpc queueing rising, KV cache hit stable. Per-token cost not relevant for right-now mitigation. traces show many short-lived requests spiking at 08:04 UTC from a small set of client IPs.

kai-se: I’m messaging Ellipsia SRE on the account side now to confirm whether this is expected (they said they were running a capacity test earlier today).

adrian-support: customer notified via support ticket #E-2019, I said we’re investigating and may apply temporary rate limits or burst.

sarah-oncall: mitigation options: 1) manual burst: add 2-4 burst GPUs to pool (recommended), 2) enable routing fallback to hosted variant (smaller model) for non-critical traffic, 3) ask Ellipsia to pause synthetic test. Which do we want first?

mike-sre: I can run the manual burst. Command: `opsctl pool burst --name ellipsia-prod --type p4d --count 3 --ttl 60m` (opsctl will register billing). Doing dry-run now.

julia-eng: also prepare rollback: if burst doesn't reduce queueing in 3m, we'll start evicting best-effort tenant tasks and enable fallback route by service gate. Config snippet to flip (one-liner): `curl -XPOST https://config/api/route -d '{"pool":"ellipsia-prod","fallback":"hosted-small"}'`

mike-sre: executing burst now. `opsctl` output: launched 3 nodes, init started. (spinner)

omar-obs: telemetry: queue depth dropping: 820 -> 340 in 90s. 95th latency down from 3.8s -> 1.1s. No obvious errors introduced.

sarah-oncall: ping Ellipsia contact (kai) for confirmation of pause.

kai-se: Ellipsia confirms they kicked off a stress ramp for feature validation. They've paused the test on our ask. They appreciate the heads-up.

mike-sre: burst nodes are Ready. GC profile fine. traffic redistributed.

julia-eng: please keep the fallback config ready but held. If things are stable after 10m we can release burst and document follow-up.

omar-obs: alert noise: 2x 429s reported by internal client libs earlier; those rate-limited requests were from the synthetic runner before they paused. No user-visible 5xx spikes recorded for Ellipsia production traffic.

sarah-oncall: marking incident as mitigated for live traffic. Keeping page open for post-incident actions: (a) remove tenant pinning or increase reserved headroom, (b) review burst policy to allow emergency auto-burst even if pinned_nodes == max, (c) schedule postmortem with Ellipsia.

adrian-support: I'll coordinate postmortem invite and change log with customer-facing notes.

mike-sre: handover to julia-eng for follow-up and RCA. I’ll remain available.

julia-eng: taking handoff — will run deeper logs and check why autoscaler respected pin config. tentative RCA: customer-side synthetic ramp + pinned capacity at max_pool_size prevented autoscale. action: recommend default emergency headroom + update autoscaler to allow manual overrides.

sarah-oncall: last check: queue depth 40, median latency 110ms, GPUs 6/9 util 30-60%. closing page in 10m if stable. :white_check_mark:

inc-bot: INCIDENT 3372104567 — STATUS: mitigated (manual burst + customer paused traffic). Followup: postmortem required.

julia-eng: created follow-up ticket CORE-5234 (capacity headroom + autoscaler override). assigning to eng-runtime.

adrian-support: doc for customer message drafted, will send after RCAs.

sarah-oncall: last_message: incident moved to monitoring. if regress, re-open thread.
